memory_verse.label: Bible Portion
memory_verse.text: "Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom. He instructed them: 'This is what you are to say to my lord Esau: "Your servant Jacob says, I have been staying with Laban and have remained there till now. I have cattle and donkeys, sheep and goats, male and female servants. Now I am sending this message to my lord, that I may find favor in your eyes"'" - Gen 32:3-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob sends messengers ahead to Esau, and notice the humble tone of his message. He calls Esau "my lord" and refers to himself as "your servant." This is a remarkable change. Years ago, Jacob had grasped and schemed to make himself lord over his brother, seizing the birthright and the blessing. Now he approaches Esau with lowered head and humble words, seeking only "favor in your eyes."

Time and hardship had done a work in Jacob. The proud grasper was learning humility. He was no longer trying to dominate his brother; he was hoping simply to be received.

There is wisdom here about mending broken relationships. When we have wronged someone, or when a relationship has been fractured, the path back usually runs through humility. Pride keeps its chin up and demands its rights; humility is willing to lower itself and seek peace. Jacob was willing to take the humble position for the sake of reconciliation.

This is the way of Christ, who "made himself nothing, taking the very nature of a servant" (Phil 2:7). Following Him means being willing to humble ourselves, even with those we have hurt or who have hurt us. Is there a fractured relationship in your life? The road to peace often begins with a humble step. Are you willing to take it?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Where might pride be keeping you from mending a relationship?
Are you willing to take the humble position for the sake of peace?
How does Christ's humility shape the way you approach those you've hurt?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, soften my proud heart. Where a relationship is broken, give me the humility to take the first step toward peace, following the example of Christ who humbled Himself. Amen.
